No tenancy or security findings.

## Review findings, most severe first

1. **Medium (PR's claims): the marker's comment says it makes the migrator apply 0032. drizzle doesn't need it.** In `0033_0033_apply_journaled_0032.sql:1-3`.
   - drizzle-orm 0.45.3 reads the newest `created_at` in its migrations table and runs every journal entry with a later `when`.
   - 0031's `when` is 1792318674319 and 0032's is 1792328555225, so a stock drizzle migrator applies 0032 with or without 0033. 0033 (1792331100117) just runs after it in the same batch.
   - The marker matters only for Lovable's own migration tool, which needs a new file to notice pending work (rule 3a; precedent 0021, 0025, 0027, 0029, 0031).
   - Risk: the journal's `when` values are not always increasing (0024 is 1790670024000, 0025 is 1790669607208). A future migration whose `when` is older than the newest applied row is silently skipped, and a marker does not help.
   - The last commit's title, "Applied 0032 migration to DB", can't be verified from the repo.
2. **Medium (PR's claims): no Verification output and no linked brief.** The body is the template; the invariant boxes are unchecked. The output above fills the gap.
3. **Low (invariants): `docs/STATUS.md:10` not updated.** It still says "0032 (T-042) written, not applied … Next free number: 0033". After merge someone following it would write a second 0033; the CI guard would catch it, but only after the work is done.
4. **Low (cosmetic): the name repeats the number, `0033_0033_`.** Lovable's habit (0010_0009, 0023_0022, 0031_0031). The guard accepts it and the file name matches the journal tag. Renaming after merge is forbidden, so leave it.

**Checked, no findings:** the new SQL adds no function, policy or grant; journal idx and `when` order; snapshot chain (0033 prevId `580190ac` = 0032's id); 0033 is the next free number and no other branch uses it (`scripts/sync-check.sh` on this branch flags its own file, a false positive); no user-facing text, so `t()` and 44px don't apply; no secrets or personal data; no CI files changed.

## RLS audit of migration 0032 as it now lands

0033 is only a marker, so the audit covers 0032 (already on `main` from PR #62, unchanged here).

"Member A" = plain member of the same account; "Admin A" = admin of the same account; "Other acct" = member or admin of another account.

| Object                                            | Op              | anon              | Member A                         | Admin A                                                        | Other acct            |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `accounts.booking_auto_approve` / `name` (column) | SELECT          | no (no grant)     | yes, own account                 | yes                                                            | no (row hidden)       |
|                                                   | UPDATE (direct) | no                | no (no UPDATE policy)            | no (0 rows)                                                    | no                    |
| `bookings.auto_approved` (column)                 | INSERT/UPDATE   | no (no grant)     | ignored; trigger computes it     | ignored; trigger computes it                                   | no (RLS)              |
|                                                   | SELECT/DELETE   | no                | own bookings via existing policy | yes                                                            | no (row hidden)       |
| `booking_defaults()` (trigger, SECURITY DEFINER)  | EXECUTE         | no                | no                               | no                                                             | no (trigger only)     |
| `set_booking_auto_approve(uuid,bool)` (DEFINER)   | EXECUTE         | permission denied | "Admin role required"            | yes, organisations only (family → `institution_only`); audited | "Admin role required" |
| `rename_account(uuid,text)` (DEFINER)             | EXECUTE         | permission denied | "Admin role required"            | yes; a family can't take a cottage's name; audited             | "Admin role required" |
| `create_account_onboarding(…10 args)` (DEFINER)   | EXECUTE         | permission denied | yes, creates their own account   | same                                                           | same                  |
| `invitation_preview(text)` (DEFINER, token)       | EXECUTE         | yes, by token     | yes                              | yes                                                            | yes                   |
| `public_guest_link(text)` (DEFINER, token)        | EXECUTE         | yes, by token     | yes                              | yes                                                            | yes                   |

- Both new DEFINER functions check `has_account_role(_account_id,'admin')` against the account passed in. `create_account_onboarding` checks `auth.uid()`; the old 9-argument version is dropped and only one version exists.
- The only anon grants are on `invitation_preview` and `public_guest_link`, both token functions already in `supabase/security-allowlist.json` with reasons that still hold.

**Tests written** (7 blocks, +262 lines in `supabase/tests/security.test.ts`, local commit `e502435` on top of `2c2015c`): execute grants per role; `set_booking_auto_approve` refusals and audit row; `rename_account` refusals, name rules and audit; `accounts` read scope and no direct writes; `bookings.auto_approved` can't be forced and cross-account booking access is refused; a person who is admin of one account and member of another can't act on the other; onboarding ignores `_booking_auto_approve` for a family. **Not pushed yet:** the push to `lovable-sync` (the Lovable-connected branch) was blocked by the session's permission check and needs the maintainer's go-ahead.

**Could not prove:** that production applied 0032 exactly once through the marker (tests run on in-memory PGlite); which migrator Lovable uses (not in the repo); the CI run on GitHub (guard and `test:db` run locally only).

**Minor, from before this PR:** signed-in users hold a table-level UPDATE grant on `public.accounts`, and only the missing UPDATE policy blocks direct writes; revoking it would make that explicit. `booking_defaults` returns early when `auth.uid()` is null, so service-role inserts can set `auto_approved` freely (intended, not enforced).
